clue.text: What about stocking books on the queen's dangerous predicament

indicators.note: stocking means holding something in stock, so the shuffled word contains the books
'about' here means turned around and rearranged, so the letters of the first word are shuffled

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first set of books of the Bible
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to make of stocking books about the Queen, a risky publishing venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but shuffles the first word, which then takes in the books; 'on' just places the queen afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in trouble, or a tight spot, is an idiom for being in a dangerous predicament.

clue.text: Poor country area is disregarded

indicators.note: something disregarded is left out, so the area letter is dropped from the country

parts.note: Hungary is a country in central Europe

explanation.surface: A poor country is one whose regions are neglected by its government.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungry land or soil is poor and unproductive; the word can also describe someone in want, lacking food.

clue.text: Surprise spell in revolt

parts.note: a turn is a spell or stint, as in a turn at the wheel
people who are up in arms, or rise up, are in revolt

explanation.surface: A sudden outbreak of rebellion catches everyone off guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn-up, short for a turn-up for the books, is an unexpected event or surprise.

clue.text: The culmination of an attempt to get up in one go

parts.note: A is one, the indefinite article

indicators.note: 'in' says the turned-up attempt sits inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: to go is a colloquial way of saying to urinate, to pee

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means rising, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is an attempt, as in have a go

explanation.surface: The high point of a climbing attempt is reaching the top in a single effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' does double duty in different senses: once as an attempt, turned upwards by 'to get up', and once as the slang for relieving oneself, which 'in' splits open.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the highest or furthest point, so figuratively the climax or peak of something.

clue.text: Type of book singled out by fellow in charge

parts.note: to elect is to choose or single out
Ron is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A kind of book is chosen by the man running the library.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-book is a book in digital form, read on a screen rather than printed on paper.

clue.text: Swan around Belgium with European trapper

parts.note: a cob is a male swan

indicators.note: 'around' turns the following group of letters the other way round

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A swan glides round Belgium in company with a European trapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns B, E and W round to WEB, which follows COB.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web is a snare in which insects are caught, so it is literally a trapper.

clue.text: Make too much of estimate on account of earlier

indicators.note: 'earlier' says the phrase for 'on account of' comes before the estimate in the answer

parts.note: over can mean on account of, as in a quarrel over money
to rate is to estimate or assess

explanation.surface: Someone exaggerates an estimate because of an earlier one.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate something is to value it more highly than it deserves, making too much of it.

clue.text: Done for finding stuff out, she breaks in court

indicators.note: 'breaks' says the pronoun breaks into the word for stuff, splitting it

parts.note: a wad is a lump of stuffing or padding
to be up before a judge is to be in court

explanation.surface: A woman is ruined after breaking into a building and finding stuff, and is now in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' splits the word for stuff after its first letter; 'finding' and 'out' only join the pieces, and 'up' before a magistrate is a British idiom for being in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone washed up is finished or ruined, the idiom pictured as wreckage cast on a beach.

clue.text: Obama's interrupted by Republican jeers

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Barack Obama's first name with the possessive gives BARACKS
R is the abbreviation for Republican in US politics

explanation.surface: President Obama's speeches are interrupted by heckling Republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is a British and Australian verb meaning to shout at or heckle, so barracks means jeers.

clue.text: Nuclear weapon Meir oddly dismissed as more limited in range

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

indicators.note: dismissing the odd-numbered letters keeps only the second and fourth of the name

explanation.surface: Golda Meir, the Israeli prime minister, oddly rules out a nuclear weapon as having too short a range.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrower means of lesser width or scope, so more restricted in range.

clue.text: Thicker grass concealing a couple of snipers on the way back

indicators.note: heading back means the whole assembly is read from right to left
concealing means hiding inside, so the two letters go within the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places

indicators.note: a couple of means the first two letters of the word

explanation.surface: Snipers hide in thicker grass as they make their way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns round the whole assembly, giving RESNED read backwards, not just the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Denser means more closely packed or compact, a direct synonym of thicker.

clue.text: Rule out admitting obstruction at end of the game

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the obstruction goes inside

parts.note: taken as the word out itself
in tennis a let is a ball obstructed by the net; also an old word for hindrance, as in without let

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A referee decides to rule out any obstruction at the end of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rule out' looks like a single phrasal verb but is two pieces; the tennis obstruction is admitted between the last two letters of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game played with a spinning wheel and a ball.

clue.text: Soldiers fetch back a former leader of the Sandinistas

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: back means the word for fetch is read in reverse

parts.note: to get is to fetch

explanation.surface: Troops bring back a deposed Nicaraguan revolutionary leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Ortega led the Sandinista National Liberation Front and the revolutionary junta in Nicaragua in the 1980s.

clue.text: Make light of foreign articles on ceremonial dignity

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article and der the German definite article
state is pomp and ceremony, as in lying in state

explanation.surface: A writer plays down foreign newspaper articles about the dignity of ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: To understate is to present something as smaller or less serious than it is, playing it down.

clue.text: Mad about getting caught after a short time

indicators.note: 'after' says the first two pieces come after the short time in the answer

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
on means about, as in a talk on art
struck can mean caught or hit, as by a blow or a sudden thought

explanation.surface: Someone goes mad over being caught out after only a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is written MO + ON + STRUCK in answer order; 'getting' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstruck once meant made insane by the moon's influence, so crazed or mad.

clue.text: A tendency once to mix it with platinum not plutonium

indicators.note: mixing stirs the combined letters into a new order
'not' means the element named after it is removed from the one before

parts.note: Pu is the chemical symbol for plutonium

explanation.surface: An old chemistry recipe: mix it with platinum, but leave out the plutonium.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking P and U from PLATINUM leaves LATINM, which is shuffled with IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Militant, or the Militant Tendency, was a Trotskyist group inside the British Labour Party, expelled in the 1980s.

clue.text: Fruit tree said to engross Australian conservationists

indicators.note: to engross is to absorb or take in, so the two letters go inside the spoken word
said means the word for the tree is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the plane is a broad-leaved tree common in city streets
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A tree is said to fascinate Australian conservationists.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the tree's sound is used, a word meaning simple; the National Trust is the British heritage charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy tropical fruit like a large banana, usually eaten cooked.

clue.text: Leonato's niece to flog diamonds without a hint of regret

parts.note: to beat is to flog or whip

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its first letter

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone flogs off diamonds without the least regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrice is the witty heroine of Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing, niece of Leonato, governor of Messina.

clue.text: Bad to defend dithering over Poins being vague

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

indicators.note: dithering is wavering this way and that, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: Poins is the setter, so the setter's name gives I, me

explanation.surface: The setter is being vague and dithering about whether it is bad to defend himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own pseudonym stands for I; that letter is shuffled with DEFEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poorly defined is unclear or imprecise in outline, so vague.

clue.text: Have one's way with academic fellow after husband leaves

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is an academic

indicators.note: when someone leaves they go, so the husband's letter is dropped

parts.note: Keith is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: Someone seduces a university fellow once her husband has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have one's way with' reads as a single seduction phrase; the definition stops before 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make it is to succeed or get where one wants to be, idiomatically to have one's way.

clue.text: Blanchett devouring work about American novelist

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing up, so the turned work goes inside the name

parts.note: Cate Blanchett is the Australian actress

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the work is read backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: The actress Cate Blanchett eagerly reads a book about an American writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was the US writer of Breakfast at Tiffany's and In Cold Blood.

clue.text: Abandon virtue

definitions.meaning: to abandon is to leave or run out on someone, as soldiers leave their posts
the noun meaning merit or worthiness

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to walk out on; the noun, stressed the same way, means merit, what someone deserves.

clue.text: Put a match to fuel left out

indicators.note: 'out' means the letter for left is taken out of the fuel

parts.note: lignite is brown coal, a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone sets fire to fuel that has been left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite something is to set it alight, as by striking a match and applying it.

clue.text: Lark's flight captured by Bill? Just the opposite

indicators.note: being captured means being held inside, read here as one piece inside the other
this reverses the order just given, so the flight holds the bill instead

parts.note: flight is escape, as in taking flight
an ad, an advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A songbird's flight is caught on a poster, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lark's' is read as 'Lark is'. 'Just the opposite' turns 'captured by' round, so the flight holds the bill rather than the bill holding the flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or mischief, the same as an escapade, an adventurous prank.

clue.text: Maria's reckless musketeer

indicators.note: reckless means wild and uncontrolled, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Maria has a dashing musketeer who throws caution to the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramis is one of the three musketeers in Alexandre Dumas's The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Pay close attention to study on school getting turned around

parts.note: to take a subject is to study it

indicators.note: turning round means the school's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A pupil is urged to concentrate on study once the school's fortunes are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To take note is to notice and heed carefully, an idiom for paying close attention.

clue.text: Dicky tried new hookup app

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters are unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky has tried out a new dating app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is slang for shaky or unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinder is a smartphone dating application known for casual meetings.

clue.text: Aware of a mawkishness Miles ignored

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so the letter for miles is dropped

parts.note: sentiment can mean mawkish, excessive emotion

explanation.surface: Someone notices a sentimental streak in a person named Miles that went unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being is conscious and able to perceive, which is to say aware.
